hunks.sol: My voice trailed off. The smell of blood reached me, and I turned toward it.

hunks.baseline: When had that happened? One of the messenger pigeons in a cage had been disemboweled and lay dead.
hunks.sol: When had that happened? One of the messenger pigeons in a cage lay dead, its belly slit open.

hunks.baseline: “It’s a method the Hidden Shadow Pavilion often uses. It’s rough on the poor pigeon, but hiding the message inside its belly makes it safer for us.”
hunks.sol: “The Hidden Shadow Pavilion uses this method often. It’s unfair to the poor pigeon, but hiding a message in its belly is more secure for us.”

hunks.baseline: As everyone stared at him, speechless, Namho gave a calm smile and continued.
hunks.sol: All of us stared at him, speechless. Namho smiled calmly and went on.

hunks.baseline: “Do we still have time to hesitate? There are fewer than fifteen days until the first of the month. If we leave now, we should be able to catch Prince Shangshan in Jiangsu at the very least.”
hunks.sol: “Do we still have time to hesitate? There’s less than a fortnight until the first of the month. If we leave right now, we can catch up with Prince Shangshan in Jiangsu, at least.”

hunks.baseline: He was right. We didn’t have time to hesitate any longer.
hunks.sol: He was right. There was no more time to hesitate.

hunks.baseline: I shot into the darkness.
hunks.sol: I shot off into the darkness.

hunks.baseline: We had a little over fifteen days left. We had to hurry, even if it was only by a single hour.
hunks.sol: About a fortnight remained. We couldn’t afford to lose even an hour.
